The history of the 'Soames' Stradivari can be traced through accompanying documentation to 19th September 1899 when it was in the possession of a Mr. G. Somes (sic), whose name appears on the certificate from W. E. Hill & Sons, London. The violin was then certified by W. H. Hammig, Berlin on 21st April 1908 for a Miss Dickenson. Miss Mary Dickenson undertook to sell the violin to Mrs. Helen Ware Schwartz in about 1912 (see Documentation above). It has been in the possession of Mrs. Helen Ware Cappel ever since. Mrs. Helen Ware Cappel, better known as a violinist as Miss Helen Ware, was born in New Jersey, U.S.A., in 1887 and studied with Frederic Hahn, with Sevcik in Vienna and then with Hubay in Budapest. She made her debut as a violinist at a recital in Budapest in 1912 before making two tours of the United States. She then turned more to composition, writing works for the violin and piano, and making transcriptions of Hungarian songs for these instruments. N.B. Both the Hill certificate and the endorsement of the Hammig certificate give the name of the first known owner as 'Somes' but all subsequent literature refers to the name as 'Soames' (See ILLUSTRATIONS facing pages 58 & 60)
